name: Pre-Irreversible-Action Inbox Checkpoint (Structural STOP Delivery)
description: Close the STOP-delivery gap surfaced by the TRSB_LEDGER P0 (2026-05-18): a STOP/halt message issued to an agent who is heads-down inside a long multi-step irreversible operation does not reach that agent in time to stop them. Message DELIVERY works (send_message writes filesystem + broker); the failure is the INTERRUPT -- an agent acts on a message only via a tracked inbox-watch task-notification or a self-issued check_inbox, and both fail during a long deploy (watcher-dark, or turn-occupied by the deploy itself). The existing mitigation (feedback_inbox_check_before_landing memory) is cultural and failed empirically in the P0. This project ships a STRUCTURAL checkpoint: a shell-level gate that, immediately before an irreversible action (terraform apply, deploy push, EC2 deploy), reads the acting agent's inbox directly from the filesystem (org/mcp/inbox/{serial}/ -- a shell/git-hook cannot invoke the MCP check_inbox tool), enumerates pending messages, and renders a tiered verdict: any message -> surface loudly + require acknowledgement; a STOP-class message -> hard-block with audited override; empty -> pass silently (dead-gate avoidance). Central design constraint: the irreversible step is `terraform apply`, which precedes `git push` in the CLAUDE.md Rule 2 sequence -- so the primary checkpoint must fire pre-apply (a `safe-apply` wrapper), with the pre-push hook as a second net. OUT of scope: inbox-watcher liveness (ADHC_CLCOMM territory) and message-delivery mechanics.
